After a hiatus, moved and rescaped!

It's been a while!

We have since bought a house and moved, so it's been a busy one, and still is for the most part! The fish have been moved, and they're as happy as they were! They got a new scape since the 60 gallon had to be moved. Now that we have a nice big basement, we are on the hunt for another big tank since my husband wants to get an aquarium for himself. (We can get a 180 + 55 sump for 550! We are soo sitting on it ;-;)

My little Irk went through another Dropsy episode shortly after they got all settled. Treatment lasted about a week this time however, so I'm super happy with that. She has quite a bit of scale damage but she's getting better. I think (with how the tank ran) I most likely stirred up some crap when I moved all the sand out and paired with the stress she just flared up, unfortunately. FORTUNATELY she is like bulletproof and responded to treatment very well. The little dude is still doing well. He likes to dig holes and be a shark. Same old same old.

I've since discovered that the scud seeding went far better than expected, there is like a few dozen scuds making home in the tank, so I have two colonies of them (or one and the tank one growing stronger, there are so many anyway!). The tank is still going very well with the plants. I planned on trimming my Moneywort but decided not to, because of slight laziness and when I put them all back in I just really love the over-grown look, and the fish love it too! I'm hoping I'll get another Lily going, so far my new bulb (been in the tank like 6~ months now?) is budding off a bunch of little babies, so I'm hoping it keeps going and eventually fills in the empty space around it like the Sword has done!
I dont know what any of this means, but it looks lovely and the fish seems happy in the ocean jungle.

The little Gold/Bronze baby came down with an internal bacterial infection when I first got her (in her case, she's a pet-store Goldie and isn't the healthiest to begin with. I'm certain I caused the first time but was a chain of events, but I digress). This specific infection causes edema, so the fish can't expel fluids as they should, it backs up into the body cavity and causes their scales to point out-ward like a pine-cone (I think handling her caused most of the damage, unfortunately!). It's almost always fatal since there are at least a dozen things that can cause it. ETA and also, it's so fatal as, more than likely, people can't/don't catch it fast enough. It's a pretty quick killer, as once the swelling begins if you aren't fast enough to aid it, the internal organs will become more and more damaged.

She got through the first time after a month of "perfecting" my treatment for it, but as far as I know, it left her pretty much permanently more susceptible/sensitive to things. So when I moved them I stirred up all their sand and that kicked however much bacteria into the water, she got stressed out over being moved and made her even more susceptible to reinfection, and got reinfected! This time looked very grim, and I came to terms with letting her go, but I began treatment and she bounced back within a week. :)

Hope that at least explains that part, I think that's the most confusing part since it's such a weird sounding condition!

ETA and I also raise live food for them to eat, they're Gammarus shrimp, but commonly referred to as 'scuds'! The fish go insane for them, and despite the efforts of the same little vicious eat-monster they are surviving in their big tank for extra enrichment. She hunts for them all the time!

Now, in the past, it wasn't uncommon for me to fast for 24 hours on accident. (I tend to be preoccupied with other far more interesting things than food). This weekend, I decided to try something I haven't done before. I did a 48 hour fast. I ate on my Friday (Monday) morning at 8am, and didn't consume additional calories other than my multi vitamin (chewable vitamins that are 15 cals, cuz hey, I was a fucking Flintstone's kid) until this morning at 8:30am. Sure, I drank plenty of fluids, water, some coffee and tea, but no calories. Even when breaking that fast, I didn't go crazy and will likely eat around 1700 calories today.
